BAGONG "UPWAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City mvw.dilq.qov.ph OPINION NO. JOHN KEVIN M. ROSALES Barangay Rosario, City of San Pedro, Laguna kebrosales@gmail.com Dear Mr. Rosales: This has reference to your letter dated 4 March 2024 seeking the Department's legal opinion on whether the collection of pass-through fees inside a subdivision by the Homeowners Association (HOA) is legal. Per your representation, the current policy of Rosario Complex Homeowners Association Inc. (RCHAI) is to collect pass-through fees from private vehicles without village stickers at the village's main gate. RCHAI has been justifying its collection saying that the fees were being collected for the maintenance of the roads and payment of real property taxes thereon. Thus, the request for legal opinion on whether this type of policy is legally allowed by our current laws. At the onset, a determination should be made on whether or not the interior streets of subdivisions were already donated by the subdivision owner/developer to the concerned LGU. Section 31 of the Presidential Decree (PD) No. 957, or "The Subdivision and Condominium Buyers' Protective Decree", as amended by PD No. 12161, provides: Sec. 31. Roads, Alleys, Sidewalks and Open spaces. The owner as developer of a subdivision shall provide adequate roads, alleys and sidewalks. For subdivision projects one (1) hectare or more, the owner or developer shall reserve thirty percent (30%) of the gross area for open space. such open space shall have the following standards allocated exclusively for parks, playgrounds and recreational use: Xxx xxx xxx Upon their completion as certified to by the Authority, the roads, alleys, sidewalks and playgrounds shall be donated by the owner or developer to the city or Defining "Open Space" in Residential Subdivisions and Amending Section 31 of Presidential Decree No. 957 Requiring Subdivision Owners to Provide Roads, Alleys, Sidewalks and Reserve Open Space for Parks or Recreational Use "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

municipality and it shall be mandatory for the local governments to accept provided, however, that the parks and playgrounds may be donated to the Homeowners Association of the project with the consent of the city or municipality concerned. NO portion of the parks and playgrounds donated thereafter shall be converted to any other purpose or purposes. However, the Supreme Court in the case of Albon V. Femand02 clarified that ownership of the sidewalks in a private subdivision belongs to the subdivision owner/developer until it is either transferred to the government by way of donation or acquired by the government through expropriation. Correspondingly, pursuant to Section 99 of the DHSUD Department Order No. 2021- 007, series of 20213, HOAs are prohibited to: collect fees, toll, or any amount from any person for passage though the subdivision roads except when it is the association that maintains the roads and/or pays for the real property taxes thereon. Otherwise stated, subdivision owners or developers are already relieved of maintaining roads once they have been donated to the local government4. Accordingly, if the interior streets of subdivisions were already donated by the subdivision owner/developer to the concerned LGU, then the HOA should be prohibited from collecting pass through fees as maintenance thereof is already lodged with the LGU. On the other hand, if the interior streets of subdivisions are not yet donated to the LGU nor expropriated by the government, then the HOA may still collect pass through fees for purposes of maintenance of the roads and payment of real property taxes thereon. Notwithstanding, the opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same, and is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion rendered by more competent authorities and/or the courts. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: A iY.J AN VICTOR .
